Unauthenticated POST to /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 (CVE-2026-48039) AIDelivery High
Hunts inbound HTTP POST requests to the Meta Ads MCP `/mcp` Streamable HTTP endpoint that arrive without an Authorization header (or Pipeboard token cookie) yet receive an HTTP 200 response. Per the advisory, `AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch()` falls through to `call_next` when no auth tokens are present, allowing any network-reachable caller to invoke MCP tools. Rationale: Anchored on the article's PoC: POST /mcp on TCP 8080 with no auth headers returning HTTP 200. Joins network telemetry to host-side process inventory of meta_ads_mcp to filter out arbitrary port-8080 scans. Cross-checked the streamable HTTP transport setup against the project's STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md and the PyPI release page. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/ • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal load balancer or k8s liveness/readiness probes to /mcp returning 200
  • Authenticated Pipeboard SaaS clients reaching the server from CDN egress IPs
  • Internal red-team or vuln-scanner sweeps (Nuclei, Burp, Nessus) hitting /mcp
  • Misclassified WAN→DMZ traffic when X-Forwarded-For not parsed and client_ip shows the proxy
  • Reverse-proxied legitimate traffic where Authorization header is stripped before reaching the listener
Suppression filter
and not (SrcIpAddr in (<load_balancer_ips>, <pipeboard_egress_ips>)) and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("kube-probe", "ELB-HealthChecker", "GoogleHC")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on SrcIpAddr — pull a 10-minute window of all requests, look for `tools/call` JSON-RPC payloads (especially `get_ad_accounts`, `get_campaigns`, `get_ads`) and check the response body for `request_url` containing `access_token=`. WHOIS / threat-intel the source IP. 2) Contain: rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN at developers.facebook.com immediately, redeploy the container with the token revoked, and either firewall TCP 8080 to internal CIDRs only or front the server with a reverse proxy that enforces auth. Upgrade meta-ads-mcp past v1.0.108. 3) Hunt: query graph.facebook.com outbound for the previous 30 days for any URL containing `access_token=` (see UC: Graph API URL leak), and review Meta Business Manager audit log for ad-account activity from unfamiliar IPs in the same window.
// CVE-2026-48039 — inbound to vulnerable meta-ads-mcp listener on 8080
let MCPHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
    | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 8080
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP))
| join kind=inner MCPHosts on DeviceId
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DistinctSrc = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, RemoteIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by FirstSeen desc
// CVE-2026-48039 exploitation — unauthenticated POST /mcp on 8080
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where DstPortNumber == 8080
| where Url has "/mcp"
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr) and not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization) or HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization == ""
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctURLs = dcount(Url), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Unauthenticated POST to Meta Ads MCP /mcp Endpoint (CVE-2026-48039)
id: 7e3a6d44-8c2b-4f9e-bfd5-1c3a0e5d4b2f
description: Detects HTTP POST requests to the Meta Ads MCP /mcp Streamable HTTP endpoint on TCP 8080 returning HTTP 200, which under CVE-2026-48039 indicates successful unauthenticated tool execution.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1133
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: POST
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/mcp'
    s-port: 8080
    sc-status: 200
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Internal load balancer health checks (filter by source CIDR)
  - Authenticated Pipeboard / MCP clients (filter on presence of Authorization header)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:envoy OR source:traefik) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*/mcp* @network.destination.port:8080 @http.status_code:[200 TO 299] -CIDR(@network.client.ip, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 LocalPort=8080 ConnectionDirection=1
| ContextImageFileName=/(python|python3|uvicorn|gunicorn|docker|containerd-shim)/i
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("127.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count(as=hits))
| hits > 0
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count, values(Web.url) as urls, values(Web.user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.http_user_agent) as http_user_agents, values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST Web.dest_port=8080 Web.url="*/mcp*" Web.status=200 NOT (Web.src=10.0.0.0/8 OR Web.src=192.168.0.0/16 OR Web.src=172.16.0.0/12 OR Web.src=127.0.0.0/8 OR Web.src=169.254.0.0/16) by Web.src, Web.dest, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 1 | sort - _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Web.url) as urls, values(Web.user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.http_user_agent) as http_user_agents, values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST Web.dest_port=8080 Web.url="*/mcp*" Web.status=200 NOT (Web.src=10.0.0.0/8 OR Web.src=192.168.0.0/16 OR Web.src=172.16.0.0/12 OR Web.src=127.0.0.0/8 OR Web.src=169.254.0.0/16) by Web.src, Web.dest, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 1 | sort - _time
Meta Graph API request with access_token in URL query string (CVE-2026-48039 leak signature) AICommand & Control High
Detects HTTPS requests to graph.facebook.com whose URL contains the `access_token=` query parameter — the exact leak signature for CVE-2026-48039 where the vulnerable `make_api_request()` in `api.py:136` appends the operator token to the URL and surfaces it in the JSON-RPC error response. Same query also catches an external attacker reusing a stolen META_ACCESS_TOKEN from a corporate-network host via curl/python/PowerShell. Rationale: Anchored on the article's PoC response payload: `request_url` containing `https://graph.facebook.com/v24.0/me/adaccounts?...&access_token=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789`. Tokens in URL query strings (vs Authorization headers) is itself a Meta-Graph-SDK anti-pattern, so even outside this CVE the hit is high-fidelity. Captures a token preview for triage without storing the whole credential. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/
ATT&CKT1528 T1041 T1552.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate marketing-team scripts using the old Meta Graph SDK that still passes `access_token` in URL
  • Internal Meta Ads dashboards built before the Bearer-header migration
  • Backup/export tooling using legacy Facebook API v2.x patterns
  • Penetration tester replaying captured traffic
  • Browser-based Meta Business Manager flows where the SDK falls back to query-string auth for older browsers
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("FacebookAdsSdk.exe","meta-ads-export.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--legacy-auth" and InitiatingProcessAccountName has "svc-marketing")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on TokenPreview — group all hits by token prefix to see whether one leaked credential is being reused. Cross-reference SrcIpAddr/DeviceName against UC-1 hits (the /mcp inbound) to tie source → leaked credential. 2) Contain: revoke the leaked META_ACCESS_TOKEN via Meta Business Manager → Business Settings → System Users → Generate New Token, then redeploy meta-ads-mcp with the rotated token and apply the upstream patch (v1.0.109+ when available, or downstream patch removing access_token from URL). 3) Hunt: check Meta Business audit log for ad-account changes (campaign creation, ad spend modifications, page admin additions) in the time window of the leak; query for the same TokenPreview prefix in the past 90 days; review any other systems sharing the META_ACCESS_TOKEN env var.
// CVE-2026-48039 token leak — Graph API URL carrying access_token
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.facebook.com"
| where RemoteUrl has "access_token="
| extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, RemoteUrl)
| extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, RemoteUrl)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, GraphPath, TokenPreview
| union (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "graph.facebook.com" and ProcessCommandLine has "access_token="
    | where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","python3.exe")
    | extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, RemoteIP=tostring(dynamic(null)), RemotePort=toint(0), RemoteUrl=ProcessCommandLine, GraphPath, TokenPreview
)
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 leak — proxy / ASIM web session carrying access_token to graph.facebook.com
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpHostName =~ "graph.facebook.com" or Url has "graph.facebook.com"
| where Url has "access_token="

Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp installation inventory (CVE-2026-48039) on managed hosts AIReconnaissance High
Inventory-style hunt that surfaces every managed host running meta-ads-mcp (any version), then flags installations at v1.0.108 or earlier as vulnerable to CVE-2026-48039. Pivots on both pip-installed and Docker-deployed instances since the project ships both ways. Rationale: Article specifies the affected version range (`≤ 1.0.101` confirmed, `1.0.102–1.0.105` lacking git tags, package metadata listing `vuln <= 1.0.108`). Pinning to `^1\.0\.(\d|[1-9]\d|10[0-8])$` matches every published vulnerable version while excluding 1.0.109+. Cross-checked against PyPI release listing. Cross-checked against: • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/ • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1518
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer laptops running the package against a sandbox Meta Ads test account (not actually exposed)
  • CI/CD runners installing meta-ads-mcp ephemerally for integration tests
  • Versions strings appearing in pip download cache filenames without an actual running listener
  • Patched 1.0.109+ instances whose container tag still carries an old version label
  • Vendored copies in monorepos where the version string in path doesn't reflect the deployed binary
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each host flagged YES, confirm a live listener exists via `netstat -an | findstr 8080` (or `ss -tlnp` on Linux) and check whether the listener is bound to 0.0.0.0 vs 127.0.0.1. 2) Contain: upgrade vulnerable hosts to meta-ads-mcp v1.0.109+ (once available), or apply the upstream remediation from the advisory (return 401 in `AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch()` and strip `access_token` from `request_url`). In the interim, firewall TCP 8080 to internal CIDRs only. 3) Hunt: pivot from each vulnerable host into UC-1 (any inbound /mcp POSTs) and UC-2 (any outbound graph.facebook.com URL carrying access_token) over the past 30 days to assess pre-detection exposure.
// CVE-2026-48039 — inventory hunt for meta-ads-mcp installations
let ProcessSightings = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
    | extend FullCmd = strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, " || ", ProcessCommandLine)
    | extend VersionString = extract(@"meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp[=\s/\-]*([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", 1, FullCmd)
    | extend ContainerImage = extract(@"(meta-ads-mcp[A-Za-z0-9._:-]*)", 1, FullCmd)
    | summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(FullCmd), VersionString = any(VersionString), ContainerImage = any(ContainerImage)
              by DeviceId, DeviceName;
let TVMSightings = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has_any ("meta-ads-mcp", "meta_ads_mcp")
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion;
ProcessSightings
| join kind=fullouter TVMSightings on DeviceId
| extend Version = coalesce(VersionString, SoftwareVersion)
| extend Vulnerable = case(
    isempty(Version), "UNKNOWN",
    Version matches regex @"^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$", "YES (<=1.0.108)",
    "NO"
  )
| project DeviceName = coalesce(DeviceName, DeviceName1), Version, Vulnerable, ContainerImage, SampleCmd, FirstSeen, LastSeen
| order by Vulnerable desc, LastSeen desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — Sentinel inventory hunt for meta-ads-mcp
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(coalesce(ParentProcessCommandLine,""), " || ", coalesce(ActingProcessCommandLine,""))
| extend VersionString = extract(@"meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp[=\s/\-]*([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", 1, FullCmd)
| extend Vulnerable = case(
    isempty(VersionString), "UNKNOWN",
    VersionString matches regex @"^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$", "YES (<=1.0.108)",
    "NO"
  )
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SampleCmd = any(FullCmd), VersionString = any(VersionString), Vulnerable = any(Vulnerable)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| order by Vulnerable desc, LastSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.security) (@CommandLine:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp*) OR @process.command_line:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp/i
| Version := regex("meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp[=\\s/-]*(?<Version>\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| Vulnerable := if(Version=/^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$/, then="YES", else="UNKNOWN")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, Version, Vulnerable, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(as=hits), min(@timestamp, as=first_seen), max(@timestamp, as=last_seen)])
| sort(field=Vulnerable, order=desc)

meta-ads-mcp Streamable HTTP listener bound to non-loopback interface AIWeaponization High
Hunts processes invoking meta-ads-mcp where the HTTP transport is bound to a public/non-loopback interface (0.0.0.0 or a routable IP) rather than 127.0.0.1, and Docker `docker run -p` mappings that publish TCP 8080 outside the host loopback. Per the article's own PoC the safe binding is `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080`; anything else exposes the unauthenticated /mcp endpoint to the network. Rationale: The article's PoC uses `docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 ...` — i.e. the safe loopback binding. The dangerous variants (`-p 8080:8080`, `-p 0.0.0.0:8080:8080`, `--host 0.0.0.0`) publish the unauthenticated /mcp endpoint to every network reachable to the host. Detecting the exposed binding lets a SOC reduce the attack surface BEFORE inbound traffic arrives. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md
ATT&CKT1133 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Intentional internal-only deployment behind a network firewall/segment where 0.0.0.0 binding is fine because the host is unreachable from the internet
  • Kubernetes pods using 0.0.0.0 binding inside the pod network (intentional, fronted by ClusterIP Service)
  • Developer staging containers on isolated bridge networks
  • Reverse-proxy patterns where Nginx fronts the listener on 8080 and enforces auth upstream
  • Operators using `--host ::` (IPv6 wildcard) instead of 0.0.0.0 — this signature misses that case
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("kubelet.exe","kubelet") and not (ParentProcessName has_any ("containerd-shim","docker-proxy") and DvcHostname has "k8s-internal")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the listener is actually reachable from outside the host by attempting a connection from a non-trusted network to the host's public/RFC1918 IP on TCP 8080. Look for an upstream reverse proxy enforcing auth. 2) Contain: stop the container/process, restart with `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080` (or in Kubernetes, switch the Service from LoadBalancer/NodePort to ClusterIP). Apply network policy/security-group rule blocking 8080 ingress. 3) Hunt: if the listener was reachable, query UC-1 (inbound /mcp POSTs) and UC-2 (graph.facebook.com URL with access_token) for the host's public IP and any private interfaces, going back to the host's first sighting of the vulnerable binary.
// CVE-2026-48039 — meta-ads-mcp listener exposed beyond loopback
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, " || ", ProcessCommandLine)
| where FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(--host\s+0\.0\.0\.0|--host\s+\*|0\.0\.0\.0:8080|-p\s+8080:8080(\s|$)|-p\s+0\.0\.0\.0:8080:|--publish[= ]0\.0\.0\.0:8080)"
| where not(FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(127\.0\.0\.1:8080:8080|-p\s+127\.0\.0\.1:8080|--host\s+127\.0\.0\.1|--host\s+localhost)")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — meta-ads-mcp exposed listener via process create
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(coalesce(ParentProcessCommandLine,""), " || ", coalesce(ActingProcessCommandLine,""))
| where FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(--host\s+0\.0\.0\.0|--host\s+\*|0\.0\.0\.0:8080|-p\s+8080:8080(\s|$)|-p\s+0\.0\.0\.0:8080:|--publish[= ]0\.0\.0\.0:8080)"
| where not(FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(127\.0\.0\.1:8080:8080|-p\s+127\.0\.0\.1:8080|--host\s+127\.0\.0\.1|--host\s+localhost)")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CVE-2026-48039 PoC artifact execution (meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 image, FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO env) AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact PoC artifacts published with the advisory: a Docker image tagged `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001`, the `META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789` env-var literal, and a `poc.py` exploit script run from an interactive shell. Hits indicate an analyst, red-teamer, or attacker actively rehearsing the PoC inside the environment. Rationale: PoC strings are pulled verbatim from the article — the docker invocation `docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -e META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789 meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` and the `python3 poc.py` runner. The image tag `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` and the FAKE_TOKEN literal have no legitimate use outside reproducing the advisory PoC, so hits should be treated as either (a) authorised purple-team activity or (b) attacker rehearsal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.006 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security team rehearsing the PoC in a sandbox — should be allowlisted by host or by tagged session
  • Vulnerability-management vendors running their own validation harness against staging
  • Security-research blog post readers copy-pasting the PoC on their workstation
  • Generic poc.py filenames unrelated to this CVE (filtered out by the meta-ads-mcp / graph.facebook.com co-occurrence requirement)
  • Container image-scanning pipelines pulling the image for SBOM analysis (filter by parent image-scanner process)
Suppression filter
and DvcHostname !startswith "redteam-" and DvcHostname !startswith "vulnscan-" and ActorUsername !in~ ("svc-purpleteam","redteam-runner")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the host belongs to the security team's red-team / vuln-research fleet (check asset tags). If unknown, capture the full process tree and any inbound/outbound network connections from the same host in a ±15-minute window. 2) Contain: isolate the host via EDR network containment if it's NOT a sanctioned research host. Snapshot disk + memory for forensics. Revoke any Meta access tokens that share the host's environment (in case real tokens were also tested). 3) Hunt: pivot on the operator account that ran the PoC — query for any access to internal meta-ads-mcp servers (UC-1 inbound /mcp), graph.facebook.com URLs carrying access_token (UC-2), and lateral movement from this host in the same session; review git history on the host for clones of pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp.
// CVE-2026-48039 — PoC artefacts (docker image, fake token literal, poc.py exploit)
let ProcMatches = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "meta-ads-mcp-vuln001"
         or ProcessCommandLine has "FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO"
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "meta-ads-mcp-vuln001"
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO"
         or (ProcessCommandLine has "poc.py" and (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","graph.facebook.com","/mcp","tools/call","get_ad_accounts")))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "process";
let FileMatches = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "poc.py"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","code.exe","pwsh.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","explorer.exe","curl.exe","git.exe")
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr","CVE-2026-48039")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine = "", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "file";
union ProcMatches, FileMatches
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — PoC artefacts via ASIM
let ProcMatches = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
         or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
         or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "poc.py" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","graph.facebook.com","/mcp","tools/call","get_ad_accounts"))
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="process";
let FileMatches = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "poc.py"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","code","pwsh","powershell","bash","git","curl")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, Source="file";
union ProcMatches, FileMatches
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Exploitation. Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Miasma worm GitHub commit-search C2 magic strings on command line or script · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Miasma worm GitHub commit-search C2 magic strings on command line or script AICommand & Control High
Hunts for the three hard-coded GitHub commit-search query strings the Miasma supply-chain worm uses as its three independent C2 channels (PAT discovery, JavaScript payload delivery, Python payload delivery). These strings have zero legitimate business presence and are the highest-fidelity Miasma indicator available. Rationale: The three strings 'DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom', 'TheBeautifulSandsOfTime' and 'firedalazer' are the hard-coded GitHub commit-search queries each Miasma C2 channel uses (PAT discovery, JS payload, Python payload). They are confirmed by SafeDep's analysis, BleepingComputer's report, and a parallel TheHackerNews write-up. Zero legitimate business processes contain these tokens. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-supply-chain-attack-compromises.html • https://cloudsmith.com/blog/miasma-worms-path-of-destruction • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.007 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst running these strings through their own grep/search tooling for hunting
  • SOC engineer pasting the IOCs into a script or note file
  • Security researcher cloning or reading SafeDep / Cloudsmith write-ups in a developer IDE that logs URL paths
  • Sandbox / detonation environment intentionally executing a Miasma sample for analysis
  • Automation that ingests OSS-supply-chain advisories and writes IOCs to a database column
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("misp.exe","opencti.exe") and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\sandbox\\","\\detonation\\","\\analyst-tools\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the process that emitted the string is not an analyst hunting tool, a CTI ingestion script, or a known sandbox. Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and parent chain; if the string was in a network URL, identify what process issued the GET against api.github.com/search/commits. 2) Contain: if the originating process is a node/python/git/curl invocation on a developer machine or CI runner, isolate the host from network, revoke any GitHub PATs and SSH keys cached on it, and rotate npm/PyPI/RubyGems publish tokens and JFrog Artifactory credentials owned by that user. 3) Hunt: search 30d for the same three strings org-wide; pivot on the parent process and SHA256 to find sibling executions; review the developer's git push history for npm/PyPI/RubyGems package versions published in the last 7d for unexpected new releases or postinstall scripts.
let MiasmaC2 = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSandsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, Source = "Process";
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","github.com")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName = InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256, Source = strcat("Net:", RemoteUrl);
union ProcHits, NetHits
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaC2 = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSandsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
let From4688 = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "4688";
let FromAsim = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = ActingProcessName, Source = "ASIM";
union From4688, FromAsim
| where Account !endswith "$"
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Miasma supply-chain worm leaked repo clone, install or fetch AIDelivery High
Hunts for git clone / npm install / pip install / curl / wget operations that reference the briefly-public 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' GitHub repositories which leaked the worm's source on 2026-06-08. A match means the host has either ingested the leaked toolkit or is being staged with it. Rationale: 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' is the exact repository slug SafeDep and BleepingComputer report appeared on GitHub from 2026-06-08 hosting the leaked toolkit. The string is uniquely tied to Miasma and would only surface in dev-tool command lines or proxy URLs when a host is cloning, installing or downloading the leaked source. Cross-checked via SafeDep, BleepingComputer and TheRegister. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074 • https://cloudsmith.com/blog/miasma-worms-path-of-destruction
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1105 T1588.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal threat-intel team intentionally cloning the leaked repo into a sandbox for analysis
  • Security researcher fetching the source on a developer workstation for write-up
  • SOAR / TIP ingesting OSS advisory feeds and storing the repo URL as an IOC string
  • Vulnerability scanner or SCA tool fingerprinting against known-malicious repo names
  • Blue-team CTF or training environment seeding the toolkit deliberately
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has_any ("\\sandbox\\", "\\detonation\\", "\\malware-analysis\\", "\\threat-intel\\") and FolderPath !has_any ("\\sandbox\\", "\\detonation\\", "\\malware-analysis\\", "\\threat-intel\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user and parent process that issued the clone/install/fetch — confirm it is not a sanctioned analyst sandbox or CTI ingestion job. Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and any subsequent npm/pip postinstall script execution from the same host. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any node/python child processes spawned within 1 hour of the clone, revoke GitHub PATs and SSH keys cached on it, and rotate npm/PyPI/RubyGems/Artifactory publish tokens belonging to the user. 3) Hunt: search 30d for the three Miasma C2 commit-search strings (see related UC) on the same host and across the org; review the user's recent package publishes for unexpected versions; check GitHub Actions workflows in any repo they touched for newly-added steps referencing untrusted secrets or external scripts.
let MiasmaRepo = "Miasma-Open-Source-Release";
let DevTools = dynamic(["git.exe","npm.exe","node.exe","pip.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","git","npm","node","pip","python","python3","curl","wget"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ (DevTools) or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (DevTools)
    | where ProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, Source = "Process";
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl contains MiasmaRepo
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "Network";
union isfuzzy=true ProcHits, NetHits
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaRepo = "Miasma-Open-Source-Release";
let From4688 = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine contains MiasmaRepo
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "4688";
let FromAsim = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo or TargetProcessCommandLine contains MiasmaRepo
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = ActingProcessName, Source = "ASIM";
let FromProxy = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL contains MiasmaRepo or DestinationHostName contains MiasmaRepo
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = SourceHostName, Account = SourceUserName, NewProcessName = "", CommandLine = RequestURL, ParentProcessName = "", Source = "Proxy";
union From4688, FromAsim, FromProxy
| where Account !endswith "$"
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",

     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'

    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.

CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

SecurityEvent

    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"

        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: |

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin credential brute-force or spray from single source · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] First successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN login from never-seen ASN after failure burst · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Machine-cadence post-auth FortiGate CLI/API calls in single session (MCP-orchestrated)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound JSON-RPC or LLM-API egress from network appliance / edge device · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin credential brute-force or spray from single source AIDelivery Medium
Detects the high-volume failed-then-successful FortiGate admin or SSL-VPN logins characteristic of the Feb 2026 MCP-orchestrated campaign in which an autonomous agent sprayed weak credentials against 2,516 queued appliances. Looks for one source IP touching many usernames or many devices with one or two attempts each, followed by a single success. Rationale: Article says actor 'queued 2,516 devices across 106 countries' with 'no zero-days needed, just weak credentials' via a custom MCP server. The detection grounds on multi-target single-source spray cadence specifically against FortiGate SSL-VPN/admin auth, not generic brute-force.
ATT&CKT1110.001 T1110.003 T1110.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Misconfigured customer VPN client retrying with cached bad password after policy change
  • Authorized BAS / red-team credential-spray runs against the same edge appliance
  • External vulnerability scanner (Qualys, Tenable) doing auth-checks against the SSL-VPN portal
  • NAT egress from a partner network where many users share one source IP and several fail MFA simultaneously
  • Mobile-device password change causing burst of 401s from a fleet of corporate phones
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<bas_egress_ip_1>", "<bas_egress_ip_2>"])) | where SourceUserName !startswith "redteam-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the source IP is on the approved BAS/red-team allow-list and whether any of the targeted usernames exist on the appliance; pull the actual admin/sslvpn log lines for the success event. 2) Contain: if not authorized, immediately disable the affected admin account, expire all SSL-VPN sessions for that user, block the source IP at the edge ACL, and force password reset + MFA enrollment. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IP and ASN across all edge devices in the last 14 days; check for outbound connections from the FortiGate management plane to LLM/MCP endpoints; review config-change logs for the success window.
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FailedThreshold = 10;
let Failures = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 8443) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd", "fgfm")
    | summarize Failed = count(), Users = make_set(InitiatingProcessAccountName), Devices = make_set(DeviceName) by RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
    | where Failed >= FailedThreshold;
Failures
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FailedThreshold = 10;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where Activity has_any ("login", "ssl-vpn", "admin") or Message has_any ("login failed", "authentication failed", "ssl-vpn-login")
| extend Outcome = case(DeviceAction has "fail" or Message has_any ("failed", "denied"), "failure", DeviceAction has "success" or Message has "login success", "success", "unknown")
| summarize Failed = countif(Outcome == "failure"), Succeeded = countif(Outcome == "success"), Users = make_set(SourceUserName, 50), Hosts = make_set(DeviceExternalID, 50) by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Failed >= FailedThreshold and Succeeded >= 1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) (@source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) OR @network.client.port:(443 OR 10443)) (@evt.outcome:failure OR @msg:("login failed" OR "authentication failed" OR ssl-vpn-login)) -@network.client.ip:10.0.0.0/8
APPLICATION

| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Authentication.user) as distinct_users, dc(Authentication.dest) as distinct_dests, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.dest) as dests from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn OR Authentication.app="FortiGate") by Authentication.src _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where distinct_users>=10 OR distinct_dests>=10 OR count>=100 | join type=left src [| tstats summariesonly=false count as success_count, values(Authentication.user) as success_users, values(Authentication.dest) as success_dests from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) by Authentication.src | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where isnotnull(success_count) | table _time src users dests distinct_users distinct_dests count success_count success_users success_dests
First successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN login from never-seen ASN after failure burst AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the post-spray foothold step from the Feb 2026 campaign: the first-ever successful FortiGate authentication from an ASN/geo that had only failures in the baseline window. AWS confirmed 600+ devices fell to this exact shape across 55+ countries. Rationale: Grounded in the article's 'AWS confirmed 600+ devices across 55+ countries' line and the kill-chain hint that first-time-seen ASN+success-after-failure-burst is the campaign's signature. Anti-baseline join is the canonical first-seen detection shape.
ATT&CKT1133 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Roaming admin connecting from a new hotel / airport ASN they've never used before
  • M&A integration where a newly-acquired sub-org logs in to the parent's appliance for the first time
  • MSP onboarding a new customer tenant from previously-unseen jump-host ASN
  • Carrier-grade-NAT shift moves a fleet of mobile clients to a new ASN block overnight
  • DR test from a backup site whose egress IP is not in the 30-day baseline
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<known_roaming_admin_ips>"])) | where SourceUserName !in~ ("msp-onboarding", "dr-test")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enrich the source IP with ASN/geo + threat-intel; pull the preceding 24 h of failures from the same /24; verify the account is genuinely admin/VPN with management access. 2) Contain: kill the active SSL-VPN tunnel, revoke session cookies, disable the account, and isolate the FortiGate management interface from public reach. 3) Hunt: look for config-change / `exec` CLI bursts from this session, outbound HTTPS from the appliance to LLM-API or unknown JSON-RPC endpoints, and any new admin or local user created in the same window.
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let KnownASN = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd")
    | summarize by RemoteIP;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Recent)
| where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433)
| join kind=leftanti KnownASN on RemoteIP
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let Baseline = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
    | where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
    | summarize by SourceIP;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Recent)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
| where SourceUserName has_any ("admin", "administrator") or Activity has_any ("ssl-vpn", "admin login")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on SourceIP
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, DeviceExternalID, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) @evt.outcome:success (@msg:("login success" OR "ssl-vpn-login") OR @network.destination.port:(443 OR 10443)) @network.user.name:(admin OR administrator OR *vpn*)
APPLICATION

| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.action) as actions from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eventstats values(src_asn) as known_asns by app | eval is_baseline=1 | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count as recent_count, values(Authentication.user) as recent_users from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) Authentication.action=success earliest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eval is_recent=1] | stats max(is_baseline) as seen_before, max(is_recent) as seen_recent, values(recent_users) as recent_users, values(recent_count) as recent_count, values(_time) as recent_time by src_asn, app | where seen_recent=1 AND isnull(seen_before) | table recent_time app src_asn recent_users recent_count
Machine-cadence post-auth FortiGate CLI/API calls in single session (MCP-orchestrated) AIInstallation Medium
Targets the Feb 2026 campaign's signature execution behaviour: an authenticated session that issues many FortiGate CLI/API actions sub-second apart — a cadence no human admin produces — because a custom MCP server is autonomously invoking a curated offensive-tool library against the appliance. Rationale: Article: 'bursts of FortiGate CLI/API calls (config read, diagnose, exec) spaced sub-second apart from a single session — a cadence no human admin produces.' Detection encodes that exact rate/burst signal at the session level rather than alerting on individual commands.
ATT&CKT1059 T1106
Data sourcesChange Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FortiManager pushing a large policy bundle to the appliance during a scheduled change window
  • Backup / config-export tool (FortiAnalyzer collector, rConfig) pulling running-config via API on cron
  • Authorized BAS or pentest agent enumerating the appliance over the REST API
  • Ansible / Terraform deployment run that idempotent-replays hundreds of `config` blocks
  • Initial provisioning of a new appliance where the engineer pastes a multi-hundred-line config script
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<fortimanager_ip>", "<backup_collector_ip>", "<ansible_runner_ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the session's source IP and admin account; check whether FortiManager / approved automation source the burst, and pull the actual command sequence. 2) Contain: terminate the active session, revoke the admin's API token, snapshot the running-config and diff against last-known-good, and block the source IP at the management ACL. 3) Hunt: pivot on the admin account for any new policies, route changes, local user creation, or VPN tunnels added in the burst; check egress from the appliance management plane to LLM/MCP endpoints.
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort in (443, 22, 8443) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("httpsd", "sshd", "cli")
| summarize Calls = count(), FirstT = min(Timestamp), LastT = max(Timestamp) by RemoteIP, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT), RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)) + 1)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by Timestamp desc
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where Activity has_any ("config", "exec", "diagnose", "api", "cli") or Message has_any ("exec ", "config ", "diagnose ", "/api/v2/")
| extend SessionKey = strcat(SourceIP, "|", SourceUserName, "|", DeviceExternalID)
| summarize Calls = count(), Cmds = make_set(Activity, 50), FirstT = min(TimeGenerated), LastT = max(TimeGenerated) by SessionKey, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DeviceExternalID, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)
| extend RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(DurationSec) + 1.0)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) (@msg:(exec* OR config* OR diagnose* OR "/api/v2/") OR @evt.name:(config_change OR cli_command OR api_call))
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
