CTFMON spawning elevated child or CTFMON-hosted privilege escalation (CVE-2026-45586 / GreenPlasma) AIExploitation Medium
CVE-2026-45586 is a privilege-escalation flaw in the Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON), publicly disclosed as a zero-day and suspected to be the GreenPlasma PoC released by Chaotic Eclipse. CTFMON normally only spawns IME/language helpers at the user's own integrity level. Detection: ctfmon.exe (or its CTF API consumers) spawning a child at High/System integrity, or an integrity-level escalation event whose initiating process is ctfmon.exe. Rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-45586 ... Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON) privilege escalation' and 'suspected to be a fix for a zero-day privilege escalation exploit that Chaotic Eclipse released under the name GreenPlasma.' ctfmon.exe legitimately spawns only language-bar helpers at the user's own integrity. A high-integrity child from a medium-integrity parent is a textbook LPE signal.
ATT&CKT1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Error Reporting auto-launching wermgr.exe/WerFault.exe under ctfmon — filtered above
  • MUI / language pack installer running under TrustedInstaller (parent would already be High integrity — caught by the integrity-delta filter)
  • Sysinternals AccessChk by an IR team checking CTF token integrity
  • RDP language input service restart during a console handoff
Suppression filter
| where ChildImage !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\"
| where ParentImage !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — confirm the integrity delta (parent Medium / child High or System). Pull the SHA256 of the spawned child binary and any registry writes by ctfmon ±60s (CTFMON COM hijack patterns write to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\CTF). Step 2: Contain — kill the elevated child, isolate the host, capture a memory dump of ctfmon.exe and the elevated child. Step 3: Hunt — back-search 30 days for the same SHA256 anywhere in the fleet (likely PoC artefact named after GreenPlasma/MiniPlasma), and pivot to the CVE-2026-45586 patch-status UC to find unpatched hosts that could be next.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "ctfmon.exe"
| where FileName !in~ ("ctfmon.exe","conhost.exe","wermgr.exe","WerFault.exe")
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("High","System")
| where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel !in~ ("High","System")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentIntegrity=InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage=FolderPath,
          ChildIntegrity=ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\ctfmon.exe"
| extend NewBase = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where NewBase !in ("ctfmon.exe","conhost.exe","wermgr.exe","werfault.exe")
| where TokenElevationType in ("%%1936","%%1937")  // Full Token (admin) — the LPE outcome
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CTFMON Spawning Elevated Child (CVE-2026-45586 GreenPlasma LPE)

PoC artefact drop — Chaotic Eclipse named exploits (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, RoguePlanet, bitskrieg) AIInstallation Low
Article references five publicly-released PoCs by researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse): YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585 BitLocker bypass), GreenPlasma (CVE-2026-45586 CTFMON LPE), MiniPlasma (CVE-2020-17103 print spooler incomplete fix), RoguePlanet (Microsoft Defender race-condition to SYSTEM cmd), and bitskrieg (CVE-2026-50507 BitLocker full-data bypass). Hunt for file writes or process executions whose name or folder contains these PoC code-names — researchers and red-teamers commonly preserve the published name in repo/binary names, and uplifted commodity attackers often do not bother to rename. Rationale: Article explicitly names the five Chaotic Eclipse / Nightmare-Eclipse PoCs (YellowKey for CVE-2026-45585, GreenPlasma for CVE-2026-45586, MiniPlasma against CVE-2020-17103, RoguePlanet for the Defender race condition, bitskrieg for CVE-2026-50507). String-name hunting is low-precision but high-recall; useful for catching unsophisticated reuse of the public PoCs before defenders patch.
ATT&CKT1588.005 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red team / pentest engagement legitimately downloading the PoCs to a test host
  • Security researchers in the org investigating the PoCs in a sandbox VM
  • Threat intel team archiving copies for analysis
  • Documentation / blog posts (.html, .pdf) referencing the names — high FP on browser cache hits
  • Wallpaper or theme files coincidentally named (yellow key, etc.)
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has @"\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Cache\"
| where FolderPath !has @"\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cache\"
| where FileName !endswith ".pdf" and FileName !endswith ".html" and FileName !endswith ".htm"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — distinguish PoC binaries (.exe, .ps1, .py, .dll) from documentation files (.pdf, .html, .docx). For binary hits, pull SHA256 and check it against VirusTotal / internal sandbox. For doc hits, check user role (red team / IR / researcher allowlist). Step 2: Contain — if a binary executed on a non-research host, isolate and capture memory + the binary. Confirm whether the corresponding CVE patch was applied; if not, the host may already be compromised at the privilege level the PoC achieves (SYSTEM for RoguePlanet/GreenPlasma, encrypted-data access for YellowKey/bitskrieg). Step 3: Hunt — pull the InitiatingProcessAccountName and look 24h back/forward for that user's other activity (downloads, browser, USB). Pivot to the patch-status UC for the matching CVE.
let Codenames = dynamic(["yellowkey","greenplasma","miniplasma","rogueplanet","bitskrieg"]);
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
    | extend low_name = tolower(FileName), low_path = tolower(FolderPath)
    | where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_path has_any (Codenames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | extend low_cmd = tolower(ProcessCommandLine), low_img = tolower(FolderPath), low_name = tolower(FileName)
    | where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_img has_any (Codenames) or low_cmd has_any (Codenames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let Codenames = dynamic(["yellowkey","greenplasma","miniplasma","rogueplanet","bitskrieg"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| extend low_path = tolower(TargetFilePath), low_name = tolower(TargetFileName)
| where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_path has_any (Codenames)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-10263", "CVE-2026-8863", "CVE-2026-45657", "CVE-2026-47291", "CVE-2026-44815", "CVE-2026-45585", "CVE-2026-45655", "CVE-2026-45658", "CVE-2026-50507", "CVE-2026-45586", "CVE-2026-49160", "CVE-2020-17103")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] phpBB password-reset Host header injection (CVE-2026-29199 exploitation) · [LLM] phpBB OAuth account-binding CSRF — anomalous traffic to pre-3.3.17 OAuth callback path
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
phpBB instance vulnerable to CVE-2026-29199 (3.3.16 and below / 4.0.0-a2) exposed on managed assets AIReconnaissance High
Surface owned web hosts running phpBB at or below 3.3.16, or 4.0.0-a2 — the versions Aikido confirmed are exploitable by a single unauthenticated HTTP request that yields a valid session as any user, including administrators. Asset-side hunt is the first step before pivoting to exploit-pattern detection; the article explicitly withheld payload details to give admins time to upgrade. Rationale: Aikido article explicitly names vulnerable versions (3.3.16 and below, 4.0.0-a2) and CVE-2026-29199. Cross-checked phpBB 3.3.17 release notes (phpbb.com viewtopic 2672170), SentinelOne CVE database entry, and Infosecurity-Magazine coverage. TVM is the cleanest pivot since Aikido deliberately withheld exploit payload until the patch window closes. Datadog/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty — vulnerability-management data is not in the listed Datadog standard sources, not an FDR event_simpleName, and not a CloudTrail/VPC/GuardDuty signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://www.phpbb.com/support/documents.php?mode=changelog&version=3
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities

  • Honeypot phpBB intentionally left at 3.3.16 by red team or threat-research deployment
  • Lab / staging forum mirroring prod version for migration testing
  • Pre-prod environment outside the normal patch SLA window
  • Vendor-bundled appliance shipping phpBB whose vendor hasn't released a re-packaged 3.3.17 yet
  • TVM scan cache predating today's emergency patch deployment
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("-honey", "-honeypot-", "-lab-", "-staging-", "-dev-", "-test-"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: for each hit, confirm the asset is actually listening on the phpBB site by curling the host's `/` and checking the HTML footer or `/docs/CHANGELOG.html`; rule out stale TVM cache from before the patch window. 2. Contain: if internet-facing, push the WAF to require auth on `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` and the OAuth callback paths, OR pull DNS until 3.3.17 (master for 4.x) is deployed; in the ACP, set `force_server_vars=true` and configure explicit `server_name`/`server_protocol`. 3. Hunt: pivot to web access logs on the same hostname for the last 30 days looking for sendpassword POSTs with anomalous Host header (UC2) and OAuth login_link bursts (UC3) — both could indicate prior exploitation against the now-identified vulnerable host.

phpBB password-reset Host header injection (CVE-2026-29199 exploitation) AIExploitation High
POST to phpBB's password-reset endpoint `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` where the HTTP Host header on the request does NOT match the site's canonical hostname allow-list. This is the request shape that lets an unauthenticated attacker poison the reset email — phpBB derives the reset link from the inbound Host header when `force_server_vars` is unset, so the victim follows a link to attacker.tld and the single-use token is delivered to the attacker. Rationale: Article describes a single-HTTP-request unauth account takeover; SentinelOne's CVE-2026-29199 write-up specifies the root cause as Host-header trust in `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` when `force_server_vars` is disabled, and phpBB 3.3.17 release notes (phpbb.com 2672170) confirm the fix. The detection anchors on the article-specific endpoint + the corroborated trust-boundary violation. Defender XDR has no native web-access-log table so defender_kql is left empty. Datadog has no standard web-access-log source in the listed schema (nginx/apache custom integrations would need a pipeline) — left empty rather than fabricated. Falcon FDR does not ship web server access logs as an event_simpleName — empty. CloudWatch path empty unless AWS WAF logs are present (not in the listed canonical log groups). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1190 T1566.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate phpBB instance reachable via multiple aliased hostnames not yet added to the canonical allow-list
  • Reverse proxy / CDN (Cloudflare, Akamai) inserting an X-Forwarded-Host but the origin Host header points at the internal origin name
  • Vulnerability scanner (Qualys, Tenable, Acunetix) probing the password-reset endpoint with a synthetic Host header
  • User-misconfigured custom domain on a hosted phpBB that hasn't propagated to ops' canonical list
  • phpBB instance bound to a raw IPv4 address — Host header is the IP, not a name
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract the anomalous Host value and the requesting SrcIpAddr; check if the value is a known typosquat (paypa1.com style) or a recently-registered domain, and whether the source IP recently hit the same `sendpassword` endpoint with the legit Host (recon-then-exploit shape). 2. Contain: temporarily WAF-block POSTs to `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` with any Host other than the canonical allow-list; force-revoke any password-reset tokens issued in the last 24h via phpBB ACP; if internet-facing, set `force_server_vars=true` with explicit `server_name`/`server_protocol` in `config.php` immediately. 3. Hunt: pull outbound mail logs from the phpBB server for password-reset emails sent in the last 7d and check whether the Reset URL contains a non-canonical hostname; pivot to victim mailboxes for the same window to see if any user clicked an inbound reset link they didn't initiate.
let CanonicalHosts = dynamic(["forum.example.com","www.example.com"]);   // REPLACE with your phpBB canonical hostnames
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "ucp.php" and Url has "mode=sendpassword"
| where isnotempty(HttpHostName)
| extend HostLower = tolower(HttpHostName)
| where not(HostLower in~ (CanonicalHosts))
| where not(HostLower matches regex @"^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$")   // ignore direct-IP probes if you want raw signal — remove this line to keep them
| summarize Count=count(), DistinctSrc=dcount(SrcIpAddr), SampleSrc=make_set(SrcIpAddr,5), SampleUA=any(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent), SampleReferer=any(HttpRequestHeaderReferer) by DstHostname, HostLower, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: phpBB Password Reset Host Header Injection (CVE-2026-29199)
id: 9a3f4b21-7c1d-4e8a-bd02-2e5a1d6e0f11
description: Detects POST requests to phpBB's password-reset endpoint (ucp.php?mode=sendpassword) where the inbound HTTP Host header does not match a configured canonical hostname allow-list — the exploitation shape for CVE-2026-29199 host header injection that poisons the password-reset link to deliver the single-use token to an attacker-controlled domain.
references:
    - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce
    - https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/
    - https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170

            - 'www.example.com'
    condition: selection_endpoint and not filter_canonical_host
falsepositives:

    - CDN / reverse proxy that rewrites Host header to an internal value before logging
    - phpBB instance bound to a raw IP address instead of a hostname

phpBB OAuth account-binding CSRF — anomalous traffic to pre-3.3.17 OAuth callback path AIExploitation Medium
Hunt for the pre-patch OAuth callback path (`ucp.php` with `oauth_service=` / `mode=login_link` / `login=external`) being hit with cross-site referrers or unusual session-cookie state — the request shape that exploits the CSRF + state-validation flaw allowing an attacker to silently bind their own OAuth credential to a victim's logged-in phpBB session (one of the two improper checks disclosed in 3.3.17 release notes; no click required on one variant). Post-patch this path is replaced by `/user/oauth/authenticate/...` so legitimate traffic should be migrating away. Rationale: phpBB 3.3.17 release notes (phpbb.com 2672170) describe two improper OAuth checks — one a CSRF + state-validation bypass that needs only a logged-in victim to load a crafted URL — and explicitly state the redirect URI handler has moved to `/user/oauth/authenticate/...` (the only code block in the original Aikido article). Inferring the pre-3.3.17 callback shape from phpBB convention (ucp.php with oauth_service / mode=login_link / login=external query params) is the closest article-grounded pivot until the second Aikido post drops technical details. Marked hunting + Medium confidence because legitimate OAuth flows look very similar — operators must tune CanonicalHosts. Defender empty (no native web log table); Datadog empty (no standard web log source in schema); Falcon empty (web access logs not in FDR event_simpleName set); CloudWatch empty (not a CloudTrail/VPC/GuardDuty signal). Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1098 T1550.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Google/Facebook/GitHub OAuth provider redirecting to a phpBB instance whose admin hasn't yet updated the redirect URI to /user/oauth/authenticate/... — the Referer will look 'external' (accounts.google.com / facebook.com) for genuine logins
  • User clicks a forum-share link from an external blog/social site that lands on a phpBB page mid-OAuth flow
  • Internal-monitoring or uptime checker hitting the OAuth callback as part of a synthetic transaction
  • phpBB cross-instance content embeds — referrer is another forum the user was browsing
  • Security scanner (Aikido Attack, Acunetix, Burp) probing the legacy OAuth endpoint as part of a CVE-2026-29199 verification
Response runbook
1. Triage: for each hit, check whether the destination phpBB instance is still pre-3.3.17 (TVM/UC1 hit) — post-patch this endpoint should be dead and any traffic is either misconfig or probing. Confirm the Referer host is not an expected OAuth provider domain (accounts.google.com, github.com, login.facebook.com). 2. Contain: rotate the phpBB site's OAuth provider client secrets in case the bind succeeded; in phpBB ACP review `phpbb_user_group` for accounts whose `group_id` changed in the last 14 days, and review the `oauth_accounts` table for new bindings without a corresponding user-initiated link event in the application audit log. 3. Hunt: pivot to UC2 on the same dest host and timeframe for prior recon, and to UrlClickEvents / EmailEvents for inbound `ucp.php?oauth_service=` links sent to staff mailboxes (the no-click variant still needs the URL delivered somehow — phishing email, forum DM, watering-hole).
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let CanonicalHosts = dynamic(["forum.example.com","www.example.com"]);   // REPLACE with your phpBB canonical hostnames
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where Url has "ucp.php"
| where (Url has "oauth_service=") or (Url has "mode=login_link" and Url has "login=external")
| extend Referer = tolower(coalesce(HttpRequestHeaderReferer,""))
| extend RefererHost = extract(@"^https?://([^/]+)", 1, Referer)
| extend IsExternalReferer = iff(isempty(Referer), true, not(RefererHost in~ (CanonicalHosts)))
| where IsExternalReferer == true
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, HttpRequestHeaderCookie
| summarize Count=count(), DistinctSrc=dcount(SrcIpAddr), Sources=make_set(SrcIpAddr, 8), Referers=make_set(HttpRequestHeaderReferer, 4), SampleUrl=any(Url), SampleUA=any(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent) by DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: phpBB Legacy OAuth Callback Access With External Referer

description: Detects access to the pre-3.3.17 phpBB OAuth callback path (ucp.php with oauth_service / mode=login_link / login=external parameters) with an external Referer header — the request shape associated with the CSRF + OAuth state-validation bypass disclosed in phpBB 3.3.17 release notes, which can silently bind an attacker-controlled OAuth credential to a logged-in victim's phpBB account. Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Asset inventory: hosts running vulnerable Pheditor (CVE-2026-48030, 2.0.1-2.0.3) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HTTP POST to pheditor.php with action=terminal and shell metacharacters in dir parameter · [LLM] Web-server process (php-fpm/apache/nginx) spawning shell or network utility — post-exploitation
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP webshell file creation in webroot by web-server process · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48030: Pheditor: OS Command Injection in terminal han
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
HTTP POST to pheditor.php with action=terminal and shell metacharacters in dir parameter AIExploitation High
Hunts the direct CVE-2026-48030 exploitation vector: HTTP POST to pheditor.php carrying action=terminal where the dir parameter contains shell metacharacters (; | & $ ` newline) that bypass the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist. Legitimate terminal usage sends clean directory paths only. Rationale: Targets the exact endpoint (pheditor.php), exact action (action=terminal), and exact bypass technique (shell metacharacters in dir parameter) called out in the article PoC steps 4-5. Cross-checked GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 and NVD CVE-2026-48030. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin running terminal commands with directories containing & or ; characters in their names
  • Penetration testers running authorized scans
  • URL-encoded characters in legitimate dir paths that happen to overlap (rare)
  • Automated backup tooling making POST requests to pheditor with cd-style operations
Suppression filter
| where csUriQuery !contains "admin_legitimate_backup" and csUserName !in ("backup-svc","monitoring")
Response runbook
1. Triage — pull the full csUriQuery / POST body; URL-decode the dir parameter and confirm a metacharacter is present outside any quoted path. Identify the cIP and authenticated session. 2. Contain — block the source IP at the WAF/proxy, invalidate the pheditor session/cookie, and take the web host offline if shell_exec output indicates command success. 3. Hunt — pivot to UC #2 (web-server spawning shells) and UC #3 (PHP webshell drop) on the same host within ±10 min, then audit /var/www and /srv/www for new .php files.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "pheditor.php" or RemoteUrl has "/pheditor"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has "pheditor.php"
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriQuery has_any ("action=terminal","%3B","%7C","%24%28","%60")
   or csUriQuery matches regex @"(?i)dir=[^&]*(;|\||&|\$\(|`)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*pheditor.php*" Web.http_method=POST by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_user_agent, Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=url "(?<dir_param>dir=[^&]+)" | where match(dir_param, "(?i)(%3[Bb]|%7[Cc]|%26|%24|%60|;|\||&|\$\(|`|%0[Aa])") OR match(url, "(?i)action%3[Dd]terminal") | eval suspicious_dir=if(match(dir_param,"(?i)(;|\||&|\$|`)"),"yes","no") | where suspicious_dir="yes"

Web-server process (php-fpm/apache/nginx) spawning shell or network utility — post-exploitation AIExploitation High
Detects the second-stage of CVE-2026-48030: php-fpm / apache2 / nginx / httpd / w3wp processes spawning shells or network-fetch utilities. Per the article PoC step 4 the injected dir parameter executes via shell_exec under web-server privileges, so the child process surfaces directly under the web-server parent. Rationale: Article explicitly states 'Remote Code Execution with web server privileges' and PoC step 5 shows id returning uid=33(www-data). The parent→child shape (web server → shell/curl/wget) is the highest-fidelity indicator that the command injection executed. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate cron jobs running as www-data invoking shell scripts via PHP
  • PHP applications using exec()/system() for thumbnail generation calling ImageMagick wrappers
  • Composer or PHP package managers spawning curl/wget for dependency fetch
  • CI/CD agents (php-fpm container running as www-data executing build scripts)
  • Monitoring agents probing endpoints via shell from a PHP wrapper
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install","composer update","/usr/local/bin/composer") and InitiatingProcessAccountName == "www-data")
Response runbook
1. Triage — grab full ProcessCommandLine + ParentCommandLine; check whether the child process invokes curl/wget to an external IP, or writes a .php file. Identify the originating HTTP request from the web log (correlate ±60s with UC #1). 2. Contain — isolate the host from network, kill the suspicious child process tree, rotate the pheditor admin password, and snapshot /var/www and /tmp for forensics. 3. Hunt — pivot to file-write events from the same web-server process for any new .php drops (UC #3), and look for outbound connections to attacker.com / ifconfig.me / unfamiliar hosts within the next 30 min.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe","php.exe")
| where FileName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pheditor","/var/www","/srv/www","/tmp/","<?php","shell_exec","system(")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "pheditor"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "php-cgi", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "python", "python3", "perl", "powershell.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("pheditor", "/var/www", "/srv/www", "/tmp/", "shell_exec")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "pheditor"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

      - 'php-fpm'
      - 'php-cgi'
      - 'apache2'
      - 'httpd'
      - 'nginx'

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","php-fpm8.3","apache2","httpd","nginx","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","w3wp.exe") Processes.process_name IN ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","ruby") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(cd\s+/(var|srv|usr/share)/.*;|curl\s+|wget\s+|/tmp/|echo\s+.*php|<\?php)")
PHP webshell file creation in webroot by web-server process AIInstallation High
Detects the persistence outcome from CVE-2026-48030 exploitation: a php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp process writing a new .php file under a webroot (/var/www, /srv/www, /usr/share/nginx, /htdocs, inetpub\\wwwroot). PoC step 5 explicitly drops shell.php to /var/www/html via the injected dir parameter. Rationale: PoC step 5 literally executes `echo '<?php system($_GET[\"c\"]);?>' > /var/www/html/shell.php` via the injected dir parameter. Filtering on .php files written into webroots by a web-server-context process is the cleanest, lowest-FP signature of successful exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress / Drupal / Joomla auto-updates writing core PHP files from the web server
  • Composer package install dropping vendor PHP into the webroot
  • CI/CD deploy scripts running under www-data publishing app PHP files
  • Legitimate plugin/theme uploads via the application's admin UI
  • Cache regeneration writing compiled .php files to a webroot-cache directory
Suppression filter
| where not (TargetFilePath has_any ("/wp-content/upgrade/","/vendor/","/wp-admin/includes/") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-cron","composer"))
Response runbook
1. Triage — open the newly-written .php file and check for tell-tale webshell content (`system(`, `eval(`, `$_GET[`, `assert(`, `base64_decode`). Capture file hash. 2. Contain — quarantine the file, isolate the host from network, kill php-fpm worker pool, and rotate any application secrets/DB credentials reachable from the webroot. 3. Hunt — search webserver access logs for GET requests to the new file path, pivot on the originating source IP from the pheditor POST (UC #1), and check for other .php files written by the same process tree in the prior 24h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www/","/srv/www/","/usr/share/nginx/","/var/lib/nginx/","/htdocs/","\\inetpub\\wwwroot\\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe","php.exe","bash","sh")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pheditor","shell_exec","<?php","system(","passthru(","eval(","$_GET","$_POST")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","nginx","httpd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".php"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/www/", "/srv/www/", "/usr/share/nginx/", "/var/lib/nginx/", "/htdocs/")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "php-cgi", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "w3wp.exe", "bash", "sh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pheditor", "shell_exec", "system(", "eval(", "passthru(", "$_GET", "$_POST")
   or ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "nginx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset inventory: hosts running vulnerable Pheditor (CVE-2026-48030, 2.0.1-2.0.3) AIReconnaissance Medium
Inventory hunt for hosts running pheditor/pheditor composer package in the vulnerable range (>=2.0.1, <=2.0.3) so SOC can prioritise patching to 2.0.4+. Targets vulnerability-management telemetry rather than active exploitation. Rationale: Article names affected package range explicitly: composer:pheditor/pheditor >= 2.0.1, <= 2.0.3, tracked as CVE-2026-48030. Direct CVE+version match in TVM tables is the cleanest way to find vulnerable assets without active scanning. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1595.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment

Response runbook
1. Triage — confirm each hit's exposure: is the pheditor instance internet-facing (IsInternetFacing=true) and is the terminal feature enabled (default yes per article)? Prioritise internet-facing first. 2. Contain — for internet-facing instances, take offline or front with WAF rule blocking shell metacharacters in dir POST parameter pending patch. 3. Hunt — for any internet-facing host pre-patch, run UC #1 (POST exploitation), UC #2 (web-server child processes), and UC #3 (webshell drop) over the last 30 days to confirm whether the vulnerability was already exploited.

          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Blinding the Watchmen: Abusing Cloud Logging Services for Defense Evasion and Visibility

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)

Unit 42 research examines attack scenarios targeting cloud logging services. Learn how to defend against log manipulation and defense evasion. The post Blinding the Watchmen: Abusing Cloud Logging Services for Defense Evasion and Visibility appeared first on Unit 42 .

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS CloudTrail StopLogging / DeleteTrail / UpdateTrail / PutEventSelectors — audit-trail blinding · [LLM] AWS S3 DeleteBucket targeting CloudTrail log destination bucket · [LLM] GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled or deleted — log router tampering · [LLM] GCP Cloud Logging log bucket DELETE_REQUESTED — 7-day shadow window · [LLM] AWS S3 PutBucketLogging disabling server access logs · [LLM] Cloud logging enumeration followed by disablement within 15 minutes
AWS CloudTrail StopLogging / DeleteTrail / UpdateTrail / PutEventSelectors — audit-trail blinding AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the article's primary AWS technique: calling cloudtrail:StopLogging on a trail (or destructive equivalents — DeleteTrail, UpdateTrail that narrows scope, PutEventSelectors that removes management/data events). Any of these immediately creates a CloudTrail visibility gap. Excludes well-known CI/CD principals so the alert focuses on interactive abuse. Rationale: Article explicitly names the cloudtrail:StopLogging permission and stop-logging API as the most direct way to blind defenders. Bundling sibling destructive APIs (DeleteTrail/UpdateTrail/PutEventSelectors) catches equivalent attack paths from the same MITRE technique. AWSService and CI-CD filter prevents the very narrow set of legitimate trail churn.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform/CloudFormation drift remediation rolling out new trail configs
  • Account decommissioning runbooks deleting stale trails
  • Cost-optimization sweep narrowing data-event selectors on noisy buckets
  • Security team consolidating multiple trails into an organization trail
  • AWS Control Tower lifecycle replacing trails during landing-zone updates
Suppression filter
and UserIdentityArn !has "ci-cd" and UserIdentityArn !has "terraform-runner" and UserIdentityArn !has "AWSControlTowerExecution" and UserAgent !startswith "aws-internal"
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the trail's prior 24h history (PutTrail/UpdateTrail) and the principal's recent IAM activity; confirm whether a change ticket exists. 2) Contain — if unauthorised, call StartLogging on the trail (or re-create via the org's Terraform), rotate the principal's credentials, and revoke any short-lived sessions for AssumedRole callers. 3) Hunt — search the gap window (StopLogging → StartLogging) in any secondary trail / GuardDuty / VPC Flow for the same principal; pivot to other accounts in the org for parallel trail tampering, and check whether s3:DeleteBucket was called against the trail destination bucket.
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventName in ("StopLogging","DeleteTrail","UpdateTrail","PutEventSelectors")
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| where UserIdentityType !in ("AWSService")
| where UserIdentityArn !has "ci-cd" and UserIdentityArn !has "terraform-runner" and UserIdentityArn !has "AWSControlTowerExecution"
| extend TrailName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).name)
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, TrailName, UserIdentityType, UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityUserName, SourceIpAddress, UserAgent, AWSRegion, RequestParameters, ResponseElements
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AWS CloudTrail Logging Disabled or Trail Tampered
id: 7a3f8b21-2f4e-46b9-a3c9-1f6e2d0c9a55
description: Detects API calls that stop, delete, or narrow CloudTrail logging — the primary defense-evasion technique against AWS audit logs.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

tags:

logsource:
  product: aws

detection:

    eventSource: cloudtrail.amazonaws.com
    eventName:
      - StopLogging
      - DeleteTrail
      - UpdateTrail
      - PutEventSelectors
  filter_failure:
    errorCode: '*'
  condition: selection and not filter_failure
level: high
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:(StopLogging OR DeleteTrail OR UpdateTrail OR PutEventSelectors) @evt.outcome:success -@userIdentity.type:AWSService -@userIdentity.arn:(*ci-cd* OR *terraform-runner* OR *AWSControlTowerExecution*)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, awsRegion, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, requestParameters.name, requestParameters.eventSelectors, userAgent
| filter eventSource = "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["StopLogging","DeleteTrail","UpdateTrail","PutEventSelectors"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and userIdentity.type != "AWSService"
      and userIdentity.arn not like /ci-cd|terraform-runner|AWSControlTowerExecution/
| sort @timestamp desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Change.user) as user values(Change.src) as src values(Change.object) as trail values(Change.command) as command from datamodel=Change where Change.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" Change.command IN ("StopLogging","DeleteTrail","UpdateTrail","PutEventSelectors") Change.status="success" by Change.user Change.object Change.command | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | where NOT match(user,"(?i)(ci-cd|terraform|backup-svc|aws-controltower)") | eval firstTime=strftime(firstTime,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), lastTime=strftime(lastTime,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
AWS S3 DeleteBucket targeting CloudTrail log destination bucket AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the article's second AWS technique — destroying the S3 bucket that backs a CloudTrail trail. Pairs DeleteBucket with the empty-bucket prerequisite (mass DeleteObject on a CloudTrail-prefix bucket within a short window) to distinguish hostile log destruction from routine bucket lifecycle. Rationale: Article explicitly names s3:DeleteBucket + s3:DeleteObject as the bucket-destruction path that severs CloudTrail's only durable destination — Figure 2 in the article shows CloudTrail surfacing this deletion in its configuration. Bucket-name patterns target the conventional CloudTrail destination naming so the detection skips arbitrary application buckets.
ATT&CKT1485 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Account closure decommissioning archive buckets after retention expiry
  • Migration from per-account trails to an organization trail with old buckets being cleaned up
  • Terraform destroy on a sandbox account that included CloudTrail infrastructure
  • Cost-cleanup deleting an empty test trail bucket
  • Disaster-recovery drill rebuilding the audit landing zone
Suppression filter
and UserIdentityArn !has "terraform-runner" and UserIdentityArn !has "ci-cd" and UserAgent !startswith "aws-internal"
Response runbook
1) Triage — verify the bucket actually held CloudTrail logs (check trail configuration history, S3 inventory in any cross-region replica). Identify any cross-region replication or Object Lock retention that may have preserved evidence. 2) Contain — if hostile, suspend the principal, revoke active sessions, and block the principal's IAM permissions on bucket APIs; engage S3 support to attempt undelete if the bucket had versioning. 3) Hunt — pivot to any cross-region replication targets, GuardDuty findings on the principal in the prior 7 days, and check whether StopLogging or DeleteTrail also ran (paired technique). Search for the principal in other accounts via organization trail.
let WindowMinutes = 60min;
let TargetBuckets = AWSCloudTrail
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where EventName == "DeleteBucket"
    | extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).bucketName)
    | where BucketName has_any ("cloudtrail","aws-cloudtrail-logs","audit-logs","-logs-")
    | project DeleteTime = TimeGenerated, BucketName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, AWSRegion;
TargetBuckets
| join kind=leftouter (
    AWSCloudTrail
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where EventName == "DeleteObject"
    | extend ObjBucket = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).bucketName)
    | summarize Objs = count() by ObjBucket, UserIdentityArn1 = UserIdentityArn, bin(TimeGenerated, 5min)
) on $left.BucketName == $right.ObjBucket
| where DeleteTime between (TimeGenerated .. TimeGenerated + WindowMinutes) or isempty(ObjBucket)
| project DeleteTime, BucketName, UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress, AWSRegion, PriorObjectDeletes = Objs
| order by DeleteTime desc

GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled or deleted — log router tampering AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the article's primary GCP technique: setting a logging sink's disabled field to true via logging.sinks.update, or deleting the sink outright. Either action immediately stops log entries matching the sink's filter from reaching their destination. Tracks both the v2 ConfigServiceV2 and admin-activity audit log paths. Rationale: Article explicitly cites logging.sinks.update with disabled=true (Figure 1 message) and the parallel DeleteSink as the GCP equivalents of CloudTrail StopLogging. Filtering UpdateSink on the request body containing disabled:true avoids alerting on routine filter/destination edits, keeping the signal tight on the actual defense-evasion intent.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform/Deployment Manager re-creating sinks during infra refresh
  • Project owners disabling a noisy debug sink during incident triage
  • Migration to a new central logging project deprecating old sinks
  • Cost-cleanup retiring sinks that no longer have downstream consumers
  • GCP Organization Policy admin deliberately rerouting org-level sinks
Suppression filter
and PrincipalEmail !endswith ".gserviceaccount.com" and PrincipalEmail !has "terraform" and PrincipalEmail !has "deploy-bot"
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the sink's history (CreateSink/UpdateSink prior calls) plus the principal's other admin-activity audit events in the last hour; check whether _Required or _Default sinks were touched (those are higher-blast-radius). 2) Contain — re-enable the sink (or re-create from IaC), revoke logging.sinks.update on the principal, suspend principal sessions, and verify downstream SIEM is receiving logs again. 3) Hunt — gap analysis: what did the sink's filter cover during the disabled window? Pull from _Required sink (cannot be disabled) for that window. Check whether project-level IAM was modified just before the sink change.
GCPAuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where MethodName in ("google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink")
| where Severity != "ERROR"
| extend SinkName = tostring(parse_json(ResourceName))
| extend PrincipalEmail = tostring(parse_json(AuthenticationInfo).principalEmail)
| extend CallerIP = tostring(parse_json(RequestMetadata).callerIp)
| extend RequestBody = tostring(Request)
| where MethodName endswith "DeleteSink" or (MethodName endswith "UpdateSink" and RequestBody has "\"disabled\":true")
| project TimeGenerated, MethodName, SinkName, PrincipalEmail, CallerIP, RequestBody
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GCP Cloud Logging log bucket DELETE_REQUESTED — 7-day shadow window AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion of a Cloud Logging storage bucket via logging.buckets.delete. The article notes the bucket enters a 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED state before final deletion — during which any restore must happen, giving the SOC a recovery window if caught early. Excludes deletion of expired custom buckets via IaC. Rationale: Article explicitly names logging.buckets.delete and the 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED grace period — that grace period is operationally important because catching the alert within 7 days enables an UndeleteBucket recovery. Bucket-name filter targets the conventional log-storage buckets (_Default, _Required) and audit-named custom buckets where deletion is unambiguously hostile.
ATT&CKT1485 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom log bucket retention re-design retiring an old bucket
  • Project shutdown deleting all child resources via Terraform destroy
  • Migration consolidating per-team log buckets into a central one
  • Cost optimization removing an unused bucket after retention expiry
  • Sandbox/test project lifecycle cleanup
Suppression filter
and PrincipalEmail !has "terraform" and PrincipalEmail !has "deploy-bot" and PrincipalEmail !endswith ".gserviceaccount.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage — immediately call gcloud logging buckets undelete or the UndeleteBucket API to restore within the 7-day window. Confirm what the bucket's filter routed (was it _Required/_Default or a custom audit destination?). 2) Contain — revoke logging.buckets.delete on the principal, suspend principal sessions, audit principal's recent IAM grants for the privilege source (was it freshly granted?). 3) Hunt — pivot to other delete/disable calls on sinks routing into the same bucket; check parallel attempts in sibling projects; correlate to data-exfiltration indicators in the bucket's retention window before deletion was requested.
GCPAuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where MethodName == "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket"
| where Severity != "ERROR"
| extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(ResourceName))
| extend PrincipalEmail = tostring(parse_json(AuthenticationInfo).principalEmail)
| extend CallerIP = tostring(parse_json(RequestMetadata).callerIp)
| where BucketName has_any ("_Default","_Required","audit","security","log")
| project TimeGenerated, BucketName, PrincipalEmail, CallerIP, MethodName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AWS S3 PutBucketLogging disabling server access logs AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects PutBucketLogging calls whose request body has no LoggingEnabled block — the API signature for turning S3 access logging off. Distinct from CloudTrail trail tampering: this targets the per-bucket access log that records s3:GetObject / s3:PutObject for data-event-style visibility on log storage and exfil targets. Rationale: Article's keyword tags explicitly call out S3 + log storage. PutBucketLogging with an empty BucketLoggingStatus is the documented API shape for disabling per-bucket access logs — different from CloudTrail tampering (UC1) and bucket destruction (UC2), so it warrants its own UC. Detection keys on the absence of LoggingEnabled in the request body.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Migration from S3 access logs to CloudTrail S3 data events (common modernisation)
  • Cost-cutting on cold/static buckets where access logging adds little value
  • Terraform refactor swapping access logging for VPC Flow + ALB logging
  • Compliance team consolidating logging targets across many buckets
  • Test/sandbox buckets being scrubbed of logging during teardown
Suppression filter
and UserIdentityArn !has "terraform-runner" and UserIdentityArn !has "ci-cd" and UserAgent !startswith "aws-internal"
Response runbook
1) Triage — identify what the bucket holds (data classification, encryption, prior s3:GetObject volume) and whether the principal owns/admins this bucket; check if PutBucketLogging is part of a Terraform plan apply. 2) Contain — re-enable access logging (target the org's central log bucket), revoke s3:PutBucketLogging on the principal if unauthorised, suspend sessions. 3) Hunt — search for s3:GetObject / s3:CopyObject from the same principal against this bucket in the 24h around the disablement; pivot to other PutBucketLogging calls by the same principal across the org; check for ongoing data exfil to external destinations.
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventName == "PutBucketLogging"
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).bucketName)
| extend RequestRaw = tostring(RequestParameters)
| where RequestRaw !contains "LoggingEnabled" or RequestRaw !contains "TargetBucket"
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, BucketName, UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityType, SourceIpAddress, UserAgent, AWSRegion, RequestRaw
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cloud logging enumeration followed by disablement within 15 minutes AIActions on Objectives High
Two-step pattern: the article frames these attacks as recon-then-action, and an attacker typically lists trails/sinks/buckets to find their target before disabling. Correlates a discovery API (DescribeTrails / GetTrailStatus / ListSinks / GetBucket) with a destructive API (StopLogging / DeleteTrail / DeleteSink / UpdateSink-disabled / DeleteBucket) by the same principal within 15 minutes. Rationale: Article describes this as a multi-step pattern — attackers don't blind-fire StopLogging on a trail name they don't know. Pairing discovery (DescribeTrails/ListSinks) with disablement (StopLogging/DeleteSink/UpdateSink-disabled/DeleteBucket) by the same principal within 15min produces a much higher-confidence alert than either step alone, and catches the reviewer-flagged enumeration → action chain on both AWS and GCP. Sigma left empty because cross-event time-window correlation isn't expressible as a single Sigma selection.
ATT&CKT1526 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security platform onboarding (e.g. Prisma Cloud, Wiz) doing discovery + selector tweaks via its service principal
  • Internal compliance tool refreshing CloudTrail config nightly
  • Incident-response playbook where the SOC itself enumerates and stops a compromised trail
  • Terraform plan + apply running both Get and Update in quick succession
  • Cloud-Custodian or similar policy bot running ListTrails before remediation
Suppression filter
and Principal !has "prisma" and Principal !has "wiz-" and Principal !has "cloud-custodian" and Principal !has "terraform-runner"
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the principal's full action timeline for the correlation window; if AssumedRole, identify the originating identity and MFA status. Check whether this is a known security-tool service principal (Prisma/Wiz/Cloud Custodian). 2) Contain — if unauthorised, revoke the principal's session token, rotate any long-lived keys, re-enable any disabled trail/sink/bucket. Engage IR for full-tenant search. 3) Hunt — pivot on principal across all accounts/projects for parallel attempts; review IAM activity in the 24h leading up to the event for fresh permission grants (privilege escalation prelude); enumerate other defense-evasion APIs (DeleteFlowLogs, DisableGuardDuty, PutBucketPolicy denying logs).
let WindowMin = 15min;
let Discovery = union
    (AWSCloudTrail
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
        | where EventName in ("DescribeTrails","GetTrailStatus","ListTrails","GetEventSelectors")
        | project DiscoveryTime = TimeGenerated, Principal = UserIdentityArn, DiscoveryEvent = EventName, SourceIP = SourceIpAddress),
    (GCPAuditLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
        | where MethodName in ("google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.ListSinks","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.GetSink","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.ListBuckets")
        | extend Principal = tostring(parse_json(AuthenticationInfo).principalEmail)
        | extend SourceIP = tostring(parse_json(RequestMetadata).callerIp)
        | project DiscoveryTime = TimeGenerated, Principal, DiscoveryEvent = MethodName, SourceIP);
let Disable = union
    (AWSCloudTrail
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
        | where EventName in ("StopLogging","DeleteTrail","PutEventSelectors")
        | where isempty(ErrorCode)
        | project DisableTime = TimeGenerated, Principal = UserIdentityArn, DisableEvent = EventName),
    (GCPAuditLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
        | where MethodName in ("google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket")
        | extend Principal = tostring(parse_json(AuthenticationInfo).principalEmail)
        | project DisableTime = TimeGenerated, Principal, DisableEvent = MethodName);
Discovery
| join kind=inner Disable on Principal
| where DisableTime between (DiscoveryTime .. DiscoveryTime + WindowMin)
| project DiscoveryTime, DiscoveryEvent, DisableTime, DisableEvent, Principal, SourceIP, DelayMin = datetime_diff('minute', DisableTime, DiscoveryTime)
| order by DisableTime desc
source:(cloudtrail OR gcp.audit) (@evt.name:(DescribeTrails OR GetTrailStatus OR ListTrails OR GetEventSelectors) OR @protoPayload.methodName:(google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.ListSinks OR google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.GetSink OR google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.ListBuckets) OR @evt.name:(StopLogging OR DeleteTrail OR PutEventSelectors) OR @protoPayload.methodName:(google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink OR google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink OR google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket))
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| filter eventSource = "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["DescribeTrails","GetTrailStatus","ListTrails","GetEventSelectors","StopLogging","DeleteTrail","PutEventSelectors"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
| stats count(*) as events,
        sum(if(eventName in ["DescribeTrails","GetTrailStatus","ListTrails","GetEventSelectors"], 1, 0)) as discoveryCount,
        sum(if(eventName in ["StopLogging","DeleteTrail","PutEventSelectors"], 1, 0)) as disableCount,
        earliest(@timestamp) as firstEvent,
        latest(@timestamp) as lastEvent
        by userIdentity.arn, bin(15m)
| filter discoveryCount > 0 and disableCount > 0
| sort lastEvent desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Change where (Change.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" OR Change.vendor_product="Google Cloud Platform") Change.command IN ("DescribeTrails","GetTrailStatus","ListTrails","GetEventSelectors","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.ListSinks","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.GetSink","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.ListBuckets") by Change.user _time span=15m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename count as DiscoveryCount, user as Principal | join type=inner Principal [| tstats summariesonly=false count as DisableCount values(Change.command) as DisableActions from datamodel=Change where Change.command IN ("StopLogging","DeleteTrail","PutEventSelectors","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink","google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket") by Change.user _time span=15m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rename user as Principal] | where DisableCount > 0
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

level: medium

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
